title: Naturality of the specified finite and completed inverse-image comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in the fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention]. For $W=X,Y$ and $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ or $\mathcal O_E$, let $\Lambda_W$ be the constant finite coefficient sheaf or the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and write $D(W,\Lambda)$ for the unbounded derived category of its module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $G=g^{-1}:D(Y,\Lambda)\to D(X,\Lambda)$ be the exact module inverse image with action transported through $c_\Lambda^{-1}$, and let $\kappa^g_N:GN\to P_gN$ be exactly the comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], for the chosen representatives and resolutions there. At finite coefficients $P_g=Lg^*$ is the derived module pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; at integral coefficients it is the ambient completed pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The specified comparisons form a natural transformation $G\Rightarrow P_g$ on the entire unbounded derived category: for every derived morphism $v:N\to N'$,
$$P_g(v)\circ\kappa^g_N=\kappa^g_{N'}\circ G(v).$$
At finite coefficients the components are the classes of the sheafified maps $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and the equation includes both chain maps and inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. At integral coefficients, write $u_N:N\to\widehat N$ for the actual derived-completion unit and $\theta_{g,N}:P_gN\xrightarrow{\sim}G\widehat N$ for the entire-cone normalization of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization]. The same specified components satisfy $\kappa^g_N=\theta_{g,N}^{-1}G(u_N)$ and the displayed naturality equation under the canonical resolution comparisons, on arbitrary ambient objects, including incomplete ones.

For any category $\mathcal T$, functors $S:D(X,\Lambda)\to\mathcal T$, $H:D(Y,\Lambda)\to\mathcal T$, and natural transformation $\rho:H\Rightarrow SG$, the components $S(\kappa^g_N)\rho_N$ consequently form a natural transformation $H\Rightarrow SP_g$.

source.place: Deligne, Weil II, (1.1.3), p. 150 and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151; explicit pro-etale/completed-coefficient argument extracted by Q97 from original steps 3-6 and 9 of lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural. The normalized comparison and common-stage realization assertions are agent-written, not theorems asserted by Deligne.

proof.text: At finite level put $A=A_{E,n}$. By [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] (a) the specified component on a complex $M$ is the sheafified termwise map $i_M(x)=x\otimes1$. For a chain map $v:M\to M\prime$ and each degree and site object, $((g^{-1}v)\otimes1)(x\otimes1)=g^{-1}v(x)\otimes1=i_{M\prime}(g^{-1}v(x))$. The restrictions give the same formula. By the tensor construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and uniqueness in the sheafification adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], these equal presheaf composites give equal sheaf composites. The same equation with $v$ replaced by a differential proves the chain-map assertion. The transported scalar action is respected because $i_M(c_A^{-1}(a)x)=c_A^{-1}(a)x\otimes1=x\otimes a=a i_M(x)$. Thus the specified maps, rather than merely isomorphic alternatives, are natural on complexes.

proof.text: At finite level both exact module functors send quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms: exactness of the transported inverse image and of the module pullback is [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], and cohomology is kernel modulo image as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Compose the chain-level functors and the transformation of Step 1 with the target localization. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the source localization at quasi-isomorphisms, with target $D(X,A)$, and with the factorization isomorphisms of the exact induced functors $G$ and $P_g$. It gives a natural transformation whose components are precisely the localized $i_M$, under these comparisons, hence the specified finite $\kappa$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] (a). Explicitly, if $w:M\to M\prime$ is a quasi-isomorphism, the chain-map equation becomes $P_g([w])\kappa_M=\kappa_{M\prime}G([w])$; multiplying by the inverses gives $P_g([w])^{-1}\kappa_{M\prime}=\kappa_M G([w])^{-1}$. The localization theorem supplies naturality on every derived morphism and the canonical comparison for any representative, without a boundedness assumption.

proof.text: For integral coefficients apply [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization] to the given $g$, $E$ and the fixed small sites. Its hypotheses are exactly the present ones: $g$ is a scheme isomorphism, $\ell$ is invertible, and the coefficients are the completed quotient-limit sheaves with their specified quotient transitions. The lemma supplies a natural isomorphism $\theta_g:P_g\xrightarrow{\sim}G\widehat{(-)}$ on the ambient unbounded category, and the entire-cone identity $\theta_{g,N}\kappa^g_N=G(u_N)$. In particular $\kappa^g_N=\theta_{g,N}^{-1}G(u_N)$ for the actual unit and the chosen comparison, including the zero shifted coordinate. Its statement also gives independence under the canonical resolution comparisons. This invocation uses the stated normalization theorem, not an inference of equality from the finite projections of a derived limit.

proof.text: Write $\widehat{(-)}=\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_Y$. By [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], $u$ is the unit of the derived adjunction $\mathcal R_Y\dashv\mathcal L_Y$, so $\widehat v\,u_N=u_{N\prime}v$ for every ambient derived morphism $v:N\to N\prime$. Naturality of $\theta_g$ from [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization] and Step 3 give $$\theta_{g,N\prime}P_g(v)\kappa^g_N=G(\widehat v)\theta_{g,N}\kappa^g_N=G(\widehat v\,u_N)=G(u_{N\prime}v)=\theta_{g,N\prime}\kappa^g_{N\prime}G(v).$$ Cancel the isomorphism $\theta_{g,N\prime}$ to obtain the asserted integral naturality. No inverse of $u_N$ is used, so this calculation also applies to incomplete objects. Step 3 gives the same component identity and this equation under the canonical resolution comparisons.

proof.text: For either coefficient stage define $\eta_N=S(\kappa^g_N)\rho_N$. For a derived morphism $v:N\to N\prime$, Steps 2 and 4 and the assumed naturality of $\rho$ give $$S(P_g(v))\eta_N=S(P_g(v)\kappa^g_N)\rho_N=S(\kappa^g_{N\prime})S(G(v))\rho_N=S(\kappa^g_{N\prime})\rho_{N\prime}H(v)=\eta_{N\prime}H(v).$$ This is exactly the naturality equation for $\eta:H\Rightarrow SP_g$.
